Section 1: Introduction • Section 2: Part-A Planning & Structure Student: Asif Billah

1. Introduction

The objective of this project is to architect a multi-page personal portfolio web application accompanied by a secure, private administrative control dashboard. Strictly built to fulfill university Web Development assignment standards, the website highlights the academic achievements, technical competencies, and leadership track record of Asif Billah, an undergraduate in Computer Science and Engineering at Daffodil International University and General Secretary of DIU Computer & Programming Club (DIU-CPC).

Purpose & Target Audience: The primary purpose is to provide prospective software engineering recruiters, academic research collaborators, and collegiate tech organizations with a fast, verified, interactive showcase of completed systems (Campus Gig, Orivo), medical AI research (Brain CT vision-language findings), and extracurricular initiatives.

Technologies Used: Semantic HTML5, CSS3 Glassmorphism with 3D Matrix Transforms, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), AJAX / Fetch API, Node.js runtime, Express HTTP framework, and Multer multipart image storage.

2. Part-A: Planning & Website Structure

Design Philosophy: The visual aesthetic balances three complementary design paradigms:

  • 3D Interactive: Physics-inspired mouse-responsive perspective tilt, specular reflection tracking, and floating depth elements.
  • Glassmorphism: Dark translucent cards (rgba(16, 23, 39, 0.72)), hardware-accelerated backdrop blur (16px–20px), subtle glowing cyan borders (#00f2fe), and electric blue ambient lighting (#4facfe).
  • Modern Minimalist: Clean hierarchy, zero distracting clutter, strict semantic markup, and responsive mobile-first typography.

Section 3: Part-B Implementation & Source Code Verification Student: Asif Billah

3. Part-B: Implementation

The application is engineered cleanly without heavy third-party framework dependencies. This ensures fast execution, clear student comprehensibility, and direct explainability during course viva examinations. The frontend utilizes standard HTML5 semantic elements (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <table>, <form>, <footer>), while the backend executes a lightweight Express service with atomic data persistence.

Code Snippet 1: 3D Mouse-Responsive Perspective Tilt (Client-Side JS)

Snippet Description & Justification: This script calculates normalized pointer offsets relative to the profile card's center, computing dual-axis rotations (rotateX and rotateY) within a 12-degree bounding limit and dynamically repositioning the specular glare highlight following cursor movement.

Listing 1: public/js/profile-card-3d.js
scene.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => { const rect = card.getBoundingClientRect(); const mouseX = e.clientX - rect.left; const mouseY = e.clientY - rect.top; // Normalized cursor coordinates (-1 to 1) const normalizedX = (mouseX / rect.width) * 2 - 1; const normalizedY = (mouseY / rect.height) * 2 - 1; // Compute 3D rotation angles & apply transform const rotateY = normalizedX * 12; // Max 12 deg tilt const rotateX = -normalizedY * 12; card.style.transform = `perspective(1200px) rotateX(${rotateX.toFixed(2)}deg) rotateY(${rotateY.toFixed(2)}deg) scale3d(1.02, 1.02, 1.02)`; // Dynamic Specular Light Glare if (glare) { glare.style.opacity = '0.55'; glare.style.background = `radial-gradient(circle at ${(mouseX/rect.width)*100}% ${(mouseY/rect.height)*100}%, rgba(0,242,254,0.22) 0%, transparent 70%)`; } });

Code Snippet 2: Secure Session Authentication & Route Guard (Backend)

Snippet Description & Justification: Implements server-side authorization enforcement. Unlike insecure client-side hiding, this Express middleware intercepts all /api/admin/* routes, verifying active session cookies and rejecting unauthorized visitors with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

Listing 2: server.js • Admin Session Guard & Login Controller
function requireAdminAuth(req, res, next) { if (req.session && req.session.isAdmin) { return next(); } return res.status(401).json({ success: false, message: 'Unauthorized. Admin login required.' }); } app.post('/api/admin/login', (req, res) => { const { username, password } = req.body; const adminData = getAdminData(); if (username === adminData.username && bcrypt.compareSync(password, adminData.passwordHash)) { req.session.isAdmin = true; req.session.adminUser = username; return res.json({ success: true, message: 'Login successful' }); } return res.status(401).json({ success: false, message: 'Invalid username or password' }); });

Code Snippet 3: Persistent Image Upload Pipeline with MIME Validation

Snippet Description & Justification: Enables persistent disk uploads for profile pictures and project thumbnails. Strictly enforces 5MB file quotas and whitelist checks for JPG, JPEG, PNG, and WebP images, preventing arbitrary file execution.

Listing 3: server.js • Multer Persistent Image Upload Handler
const storage = multer.diskStorage({ destination: (req, file, cb) => cb(null, path.join(__dirname, 'public', 'uploads')), filename: (req, file, cb) => { const ext = path.extname(file.originalname).toLowerCase(); const sanitized = path.basename(file.originalname, ext).replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '_'); cb(null, `${sanitized}-${Date.now()}${ext}`); } }); const upload = multer({ storage: storage, limits: { fileSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024 }, // 5 MB limit fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => { const allowed = /jpeg|jpg|png|webp/; const valid = allowed.test(path.extname(file.originalname).toLowerCase()) && allowed.test(file.mimetype); valid ? cb(null, true) : cb(new Error('Only JPG, JPEG, PNG, and WebP formats supported!')); } });
Academic Explanation for Course Teacher: The combination of Multer disk storage and JSON synchronization ensures that uploaded pictures remain completely persistent across server reboots, fulfilling the strict university instruction forbidding temporary blob URLs or ephemeral localStorage.

4. Part-C: Form, Testing & Justification

Contact Form Implementation: Features all seven mandated input elements: (1) Full Name (text), (2) Email (regex validated), (3) Category dropdown, (4) Contact method radio buttons, (5) Checkboxes for interests, (6) Message textarea, and (7) Submit button with an asynchronous AJAX spinner.

Cross-Browser Testing: Chrome vs. Firefox Observations

Testing Feature Google Chrome (v131+) Mozilla Firefox (v132+) Compatibility Resolution Applied
Backdrop Filter Blur Rendered seamlessly with zero performance stutter. Supported flawlessly; required standard CSS rule. Added both backdrop-filter and -webkit-backdrop-filter.
3D CSS Card Transforms Smooth 60fps tracking on perspective(1200px). Occasional subpixel text jitter during transforms. Added backface-visibility: hidden and transform: translateZ(0).
HTML5 Form Validation Native bubble popups trigger correctly on invalid email. Native tooltips match browser theme styling. Integrated custom JavaScript validation banner for unified UI.
Image Upload & Preview FileReader DataURL displays instantly in preview. Identical instantaneous preview performance. Sanitized filename regex for cross-platform OS filesystem safety.

Two Real Development Problems & Implemented Solutions

Problem 1: Mouse Tilt Jitter During CSS Keyframe Floating Animation: When hovering over the 3D profile card, the continuous CSS @keyframes floatCard animation fought with the JavaScript mousemove inline transform, producing violent optical stutter.
Solution: Implemented a dynamic mouseenter listener that sets animationPlayState = 'paused' and smoothly resumes the idle animation after cursor departure using a 600ms cubic-bezier transition.

Problem 2: Multer File Upload Asynchrony & Stale Image Path Binding: Initial upload implementations experienced race conditions where the database updated before the uploaded image finished flushing to disk.
Solution: Refactored the upload pipeline to execute Multer's single-file middleware synchronously, returning the finalized server path /uploads/filename.ext to the client before updating data/portfolio.json.

Justification of Design & Semantic HTML Structure

Using semantic elements (<article>, <nav>, <table>) provides screen readers with accessible structural hierarchy while boosting SEO scores. The dark glassmorphism theme matches modern tech industry aesthetics and eases reading strain.

5. Conclusion & Learning Outcomes

Through this university project, I successfully bridged modern frontend design concepts (3D transforms, glassmorphic optics) with reliable backend systems (session authentication, file streaming, atomic JSON storage). I gained valuable mastery in cross-browser compatibility debugging, asynchronous event loop management, and clean codebase architecture.
